notes.title: Vote for the Indie of The Year!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/1007504/02201fe3814433c0cae00220412cdd69bf6937b0.png[/img]

Hey Guys, 

Back for an 9th time, it's the 2018 Indie of the Year Awards, celebarating the best games released this year. 

In 2016, Epistory had the chance to win the Best Early Access Award. Thanks again to the community for that! ːepipartyː

This year, we have two of our games competing for Indie of the Year Awards. So, if you think that they deserves to be the Indie of The Year on Indie DB, it is up to you to vote for your favorite indie games so that they may make the top 100 which will be announced on the 11th of December. [b]The voting process doesn't require to login[/b]; you just have to follow the link and click on VOTE. ːpalwinkː

If you feel like you would prefer to vote for other indie games than ours, please do it! All indies need support and love! So, feel free to visit their indie DB page and vote for them ːshiftheartː

Thank you! 

VirginRedemption

notes.title: Let's chat at Gamescom 2018
notes.content:
Hey guys! 

This year again, we are proud to be part of the Indie Arena Booth (Hall 10) at Gamescom 2018 showcasing one last time [b]Shift Quantum[/b]. 

As announced on our [url=https://discord.gg/KqtBnHM]Discord[/url], we'll start soon to communicate about our next typing game which as the code name "[b]Typing 2[/b]", until we reveal the name of the game in September. We'll be glad to have a little chat about it and gather your ideas during Gamescom too. 

Don't hesitate to drop by. The Indie Arena Booth the right place to discover wonderful indie games you've probably never heard of. 

Here's the level of Shift Quantum we've created for Gamescom. Cheers!

notes.title: Epistory dev s Algo Bot swaps typing for coding
notes.content:
I’ve never entirely understood the appeal of games featuring programming elements. They ask you to enact one of the trickiest parts of development, but without rewarding you with a finished game at the end. Algo Bot – a new puzzler from the developers of horsey type-’em-up Epistory, which Pip enjoyed a fair bit – features programming, but wraps it up in an attractive sci-fi world where WALL-E-esque robots bicker in gleaming spaceship hallways. It’s out now on Steam for $8.99/$6.47.
